html:
Canadian Steel l stud framing sizes refers to the construction of walls and planes using cold-formed steel components. There are two main components of Steel stud framing, a stud and a track. Heavier gauge Steel studs are used in load bearing walls and structural applications such as exterior walls. Lighter gauge Steel studs are used in non-load bearing applications such as some interior walls, half-walls, and partitions.

Canadian Light Gauge Steel Stud Framing Sizes

Light gauge steel stud framing used for interior wall partitions in Canada comes in various shapes, thicknesses, sizes, and finishes. Each of these components has a specific function in the wall assembly. Selecting the correct size and thickness will depend primarily on the spacing of the framing members and the height of the wall. Steel studs framing manufactured lengths in Canada ranging from 8′-0″ to 24′-0″ and tracks which come in 10′-0″ lengths. The thicknesses of steel used here range from about 1 to 3mm for structural sections, and 1 to 2mm for non-structural sections. The members are sized to roughly correspond to wood members: 2″x4″ and 2″x6″ are common sizes. Their higher strength allows greater spacing between members when compared to wood frame construction: about 24″ (600mm) for LGS vs. about 16″ or 20″ (400 or 500mm) for wood. Fewer members translates to quicker construction times.
